why: Despite the package name, this is not a workflow/scheduling harness - it's a stateless prompt-to-skill classifier for one person's ~35-skill catalog, wired into a UserPromptSubmit hook that must fail-safe to '{}' with no network call. None of the task's ten named libraries do prompt routing; category mismatch. The real comparison class - semantic-router, LLM-based classification, Rasa/snips-nlu NLU - trades a deterministic, tested regex table for an embedding dependency, a per-turn model call, or a training pipeline, none proportionate to a hand-curated route list.

alternatives.name: semantic-router (aurelio-labs)
alternatives.covers: Embedding-similarity based routing of text to named routes; can run fully local with local encoders. Confirmed active: release dated 2026-05-23.
alternatives.gap: Adds an embedding-model runtime + non-determinism a golden-tested regex table doesn't have; no built-in EN/HE/AR low-confidence phrase list or FTS corpus-snippet retrieval, both would need to be rebuilt alongside it.
alternatives.cost: New dependency + a local encoder model to keep it offline.
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained MIT project, recent 2026 activity (confirmed via WebSearch).

alternatives.name: LLM-based intent classification (ask the model itself)
alternatives.covers: A single model call classifies the prompt into a skill/persona instead of regex matching.
alternatives.gap: Runs on every UserPromptSubmit turn; needs network + a model call, which the hook's own contract avoids ('always exit 0, fail safe to {}'); recurring cost against the no-paid-services constraint.
alternatives.cost: Per-turn latency + token spend; a new failure mode (model unavailable) in a hook that must never block the prompt.
alternatives.maturity: Well-understood pattern (LLM routing chains), not a specific packaged library.

alternatives.name: Rasa NLU / snips-nlu style frameworks
alternatives.covers: Trained intent-classification NLU with slots, confidence scores, entity extraction.
alternatives.gap: Needs training data + a retraining step for every new skill; disproportionate to a ~35-route personal keyword table one person edits directly.
alternatives.cost: Training pipeline, model artifacts, retrain-on-change workflow.
alternatives.maturity: Rasa mature but heavyweight; snips-nlu largely dormant.

alternatives.name: transitions / python-statemachine (the task's named FSM libraries)
alternatives.covers: State machines - modeling states and legal transitions between them.
alternatives.gap: Does not apply: router.py has no states to model; it is a stateless classify-and-annotate function over free text, not a state graph, so these are the wrong tool category entirely.

evidence: Read router.py (306 ln) and self_improve.py (41 ln) in full. Confirmed callers: dot-claude/hooks/prompt-router.sh and dot-codex/hooks/prompt-router.sh exec `python -m intent_control_plane.harness.router`; dot-claude/bin/self-improve.py imports routed_skill_names/build_reflect_prompt/unreachable_skills (ln28-29). WebSearch: semantic-router last released 2026-05-23; not run/tested.
recheck: grep -rn "harness.router|harness.self_improve" claude-setup --include=*.sh --include=*.py -- confirms the hook wiring is still live before trusting keep-ours again.
migration_loc: 0 lines (no action, keep-ours). If replaced with semantic-router: est. -150 src / +80 (drop regex table, add route+local-encoder config), plus a new model-runtime dependency to vet for offline CI.
what_ours_does: router.py (305 ln): regex classifier for the UserPromptSubmit hook - matches prompt vs ~35 curated patterns to suggest skills + a gastown persona, flags low-confidence EN/HE/AR phrasing, pulls FTS5 corpus snippets, ranks by usage telemetry. self_improve.py (40 ln): set-diff of installed vs reachable skills + a Codex-reflect prompt builder. Both wired into the live hook shim + self-improve script.
strongest_counterargument: It's still 305 lines of hand-maintained regex/persona/telemetry logic for something the already-running model could arguably classify in less code, with no regex-drift risk (self_improve.py exists solely to catch stale routes). The audit's prior says hand-rolled infra should lose by default, and this verdict rests on the alternatives being worse-shaped, not on proving this shape is load-bearing.
